shards.title: Runtime context identity and head collection
shards.purpose: Own the shared context object, extension-slot visibility, React provider wrapper and head collector edge as one identity-sensitive module; these files directly import each other.
shards.target_scope: Fork additions belong in runtime-extensions behind a proved native runtime/React seam. Preserve the public RuntimeContext object identity. This shard owns the inventory export identity src/exports/head.ts, including removal of its @modern-js/runtime-extensions edge; packaging applies resulting package-export changes.
prerequisites: Read-only route audit can start immediately from recorded identities; reconcile against the selected integration head before accepting file dispositions. Source writes require this shard's own evidence-backed lawful route and exact source/destination reservation, not completion of a global ownership wave.

Prove whether existing RuntimePlugin wrapping/SSR collector hooks can host the context and head behavior without a governed upstream-to-fork import. The current symbol slot is an implementation, not an already approved upstream interface.

Agree only the extension accessor and context projection contract needed by router-realms-prefetch; agree head-record/Helmet state and RSC serialization contract with runtime-ssr. Independent context/head auditing needs neither lane to finish.

If audited runtime.ts, wrapper.tsx or import-only exports/head.ts cannot meet the complete-PR 20 added-plus-removed line cap, prepare a neutral upstream proposal and record the external landing dependency; do not rename the identity or retain a concealed import.
verification: Run context extension, wrapper and head suites after lawful relocation. Preserve cross-copy accessor coherence, per-request isolation, no internal state in public enumeration/serialization, stable React context identity and server/client head behavior.
Pair with SSR collector owner for stream/string and RSC coverage. Scan both direct and re-export dependencies; exports/head must have zero governed edges.
shards.stop_condition: All nine reserved identities have proved disposition and tests remain exercised; stop this shard if the public-context or collector seam requires unresolved upstream changes. Other workers can continue.

shards.title: Native router providers, lifecycle and prefetch
shards.purpose: Keep provider registration, app-owned realms, lifecycle snapshots and Link/preload behavior together because all consume the same runtime/router identity and isolation contract.
shards.target_scope: Move genuine fork routing behavior to plugin-tanstack and/or runtime-extensions using native router/runtime plugin hooks. Own PrefetchLink.tsx and its existing audited tests as identities, not freely movable fork files.
prerequisites: Read-only route audit can start immediately from recorded identities; reconcile against the selected integration head before accepting file dispositions. Source writes require this shard's own evidence-backed lawful route and exact source/destination reservation, not completion of a global ownership wave.

Prove provider hook registration and framework resolution against the actual router runtime plugin; negotiate exact lifecycle snapshot/accessor contract with context-head and cleanup/hydration consumers in runtime-ssr.

Prove native Link/NavLink and TanStack preload integration without click interception, synthetic anchor handlers or app navigation wrappers. The current PrefetchLink dependency on runtime-extensions is an edge to remove, not a reusable legal seam.

Source relocation can proceed after its local interfaces are frozen. Integration of a neutral upstream provider or prefetch seam must wait for its actual acceptance if the full-PR per-file 20-line cap cannot accommodate the lawful caller patch.
verification: Run lifecycle, provider, internalProvider, provider-realm-isolation, plugin.client, prefetch, prefetch-realm-isolation, routerHelper and utils suites. Preserve cancellation, native modified-click/defaultPrevented behavior, app-owned provider realms, cleanup and cross-shell isolation.

Verify native TanStack/React/router identity on real bundles; remove the PrefetchLink governed import edge. Include all prior PR changes when measuring audited PrefetchLink.tsx, utils.tsx and their audited tests.
shards.stop_condition: Every reserved routing identity is repaired under its own legal route and native behavior proofs pass. An over-cap PrefetchLink or provider seam blocks this shard's integration, not federation/debugger/CLI audits.

shards.title: Federated surface consumption and recovery
shards.purpose: Own the module-federation directory and matching tests as a cohesive API: its index contains telemetry behavior and re-exports, consume-surface imports that index, and distributed SSR reads runtime context.
shards.target_scope: Genuine fork-owned runtime extension modules for consumption, distributed fragments, last-known-good and manifest recovery. Preserve delivery-unit identity and required degradation policy; do not grow an upstream runtime package subsystem.
prerequisites: Read-only route audit can start immediately from recorded identities; reconcile against the selected integration head before accepting file dispositions. Source writes require this shard's own evidence-backed lawful route and exact source/destination reservation, not completion of a global ownership wave.
Prove native RuntimePlugin/federation registration entrypoints and exact destination modules. Negotiate toolkit surface-resolution/discovery exports and the wait utility with toolkit owners.

Agree runtime context access for distributed SSR with context-head and fragment locals/resolution contract with server/SSR owners. This can happen while each peer audits; whole peer completion is unnecessary.

Retain current emergency-age/last-known-good security policy until separate evidence and product authorization permit retirement. A missing required upstream extension is an explicit external dependency for the affected integration, not a reason to silently change behavior.
verification: Run all module-federation suites including node child-process recovery fixture. Exercise mandatory degraded state, critical failure propagation, bounded retry/timeout, non-retryable contract/identity failures, last-known-good validity and distributed fragment isolation.
Verify browser/Node packaging and actual public-export identity, including the index/consume-surface cycle. Preserve complete delivery-unit metadata through the toolkit handoff.
shards.stop_condition: All reserved federation implementations and tests leave governed upstream locations through proved ownership routes, with no duplicate implementation retained. Required fragment or discovery contract changes remain explicit handoffs.

shards.title: Browser boundary debugger plugin
shards.purpose: The debugger implementation and its three dedicated tests form an independent browser instrumentation plugin with a RuntimePlugin type dependency; it does not need router/provider or SSR internals to be redesigned first.
shards.target_scope: Fork-owned runtime-extensions browser instrumentation module registered through the existing runtime plugin seam, subject to confirming that seam in the local route audit.
prerequisites: Read-only route audit can start immediately from recorded identities; reconcile against the selected integration head before accepting file dispositions. Source writes require this shard's own evidence-backed lawful route and exact source/destination reservation, not completion of a global ownership wave.

Prove RuntimePlugin registration and browser/server export conditions for the debugger, plus the current metadata and data-modern-boundary-id DOM contract. No blanket context/router completion dependency.
Obtain an exact destination/export reservation and provide packaging with its registration/export patch; coordinate generated-surface consumer import updates via their owner.
verification: Run browser, client and index debugger tests in isolated environments; verify localStorage failure handling, visibility/labels, event/listener cleanup and SSR-safe import behavior.
Check real browser packaging includes the plugin through native registration and preserves Tractor's visible UI.
shards.stop_condition: All four debugger identities have lawful disposition, native registration and passing browser/server import proofs; no router or federation completion is required if existing contracts suffice.

shards.title: Runtime CLI generation, RSC boundary and test harness
shards.purpose: Own build-time runtime entry contracts and their regression fixtures, plus the shared runtime test/type configuration identity. Coordinate configuration patches centrally instead of having every module worker edit the same harness.
shards.target_scope: Fork-owned CLI/runtime integration behind proved native CLI generator hooks; retain necessary native entrypoint contracts. Own rstest.config.mts and tsconfig.tsgo.json inventory identities and collect other shards' harness requirements. Do not hand-edit generated outputs.
prerequisites: Read-only route audit can start immediately from recorded identities; reconcile against the selected integration head before accepting file dispositions. Source writes require this shard's own evidence-backed lawful route and exact source/destination reservation, not completion of a global ownership wave.

Audit actual CLI router entry/handler hooks, atomic nested-routes spec writes, document bundler hooks and RSC worker entry/export conditions before writes. Coordinate app-tools/build owner only for those actual seams.

Reconcile absent packages/runtime/plugin-runtime/scripts/gen-static.ts against baseline provenance and any rename/deletion; absence does not discharge its audited identity or confer permission to recreate generated files.

Prove legal per-file treatment for document/cli/index.ts, rstest.config.mts and gen-static.ts; any required upstream CLI seam beyond the 20-line complete-PR allowance has a real external acceptance dependency. Other shards may run existing tests before harness integration.
verification: Run registry surface, router CLI extension, RSC build boundary and RSC router payload suites; compile actual RSC on/off fixtures and verify worker/browser/Node export resolution.

Validate atomic nested-routes updates and unchanged native route generation. Run affected runtime test environments and type checks after consolidating harness patches, without excluding failures or changing app config to conceal framework defects.
shards.stop_condition: Every reserved CLI/RSC/config identity, including the absent generator identity, has accounted provenance and lawful disposition. Shared harness consumes module handoffs once; unresolved upstream hooks block only dependent writes/integration.

shards.title: SSR and hydration regression ownership
shards.purpose: Own the runtime-router inventory tests that exercise SSR/browser implementations assigned elsewhere. This is a concrete regression migration worker with existing files, not a second owner of SSR production code.
shards.target_scope: Relocate genuine fork-owned regression tests to the proved runtime-extensions/native seam owners and preserve real bundle coverage. Source implementations remain with runtime-ssr or the explicitly identified current owner.
prerequisites: Read-only route audit can start immediately from recorded identities; reconcile against the selected integration head before accepting file dispositions. Source writes require this shard's own evidence-backed lawful route and exact source/destination reservation, not completion of a global ownership wave.
Immediately audit assertions, imports, fixture setup and required failure cases in these existing tests. Prove destination test ownership independently; no need to wait for all runtime-ssr routes.

For each migrated suite, wait only for the exact implementation/export seam it imports: hydration/loadable compiler contract, request-response cleanup, CSS/script serialization, string rendering or context/head collection.

Coordinate router-realms-prefetch snapshot/cleanup fixture contract and context-head Helmet/context identity. If implementation is blocked on upstream, retain the proof against an exact proposal and label it non-integratable until landing.
verification: Run all reserved suites at their lawful destinations. Preserve bundled chunkLoadingGlobal behavior, exactly-once cleanup/cancellation, redirects/headers, script ordering and escaping, federated CSS escaping, Helmet collection and callable loadable CJS interop.
Use the existing real Rspack hydration bundle proof in addition to unit mocks. Report unchanged or stronger assertions and no loss of test discovery when old paths are deleted.
shards.stop_condition: Every reserved regression identity is accounted for and remains executable against the final owning implementation. Tests cannot pass by deleting assertions, weakening selectors or keeping copied framework logic in fixtures.

notes: Planning artifact only; source writes, upstream submission, git/br mutations, merge and release are not authorized by this artifact. Six independent read-only route audits can start immediately. Source worker release is per proved module seam; do not turn local interface agreement into a global freeze gate.

Coverage: 62 divergence rows plus 2 import edges yield 63 unique input identities. PrefetchLink.tsx owns one divergence row and its import edge in router-realms-prefetch; import-only exports/head.ts is owned once in context-head. Files are disjoint across shards.

All manifests, package export maps, lockfile, cohort/release changes, ledger and both distinct boundary allowlists are integration-owned. A handoffs path is a coordination point, never a second write reservation. Inventory-owned source export identities stay assigned to their shard with explicit packaging handoff.

Fork-created inventory files must move into genuine fork-owned packages or be lawfully deleted; moving an audited identity retains its provenance. Every affected audited file has a hard 20 added-plus-removed line cap across the complete eventual PR, including PR49 and subsequent edits, plus the fixed-base cumulative hunk/line budgets. Non-shrink changes require same-PR ledger evidence. No worker/worktree/split PR creates a fresh budget for the same combined merge range.

Actual upstream acceptance is an external prerequisite only where the local audit proves an existing seam/capped patch insufficient. Code against a prepared proposal is provisional. Provenance carry-forward and package integration cannot treat a proposal as landed; no alias/re-export/dynamic-import hiding or scope reset is permitted.

True coupling: runtime context symbols and React object identity cross context/router/SSR; router snapshots and cleanup cross router/SSR tests; federation delivery units cross toolkit/server; CLI fixtures compile RSC/render exports. The debugger has an existing RuntimePlugin-shaped seam and can proceed independently if confirmed.

Inventory is historical: scripts/gen-static.ts is absent in this checkout and remains explicitly owned by cli-rsc-harness until canonical baseline reconciliation proves its disposition. Destination files and any additional discovered caller identities need explicit reservations before source edits.

After component proofs, integration runs the complete canonical divergence and imports gates without selected roots/alternate scope. Final ERP/Tractor source and published acceptance belongs to program acceptance owners; shared-host driver ports remain a real serialization constraint.
